items.item_text: Legal Right to work in the United States
California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act
Masters degree in higher education leadership, counseling, or related field, or equivalent experience/training

Knowledge of first-year student success principles and strategies, with demonstrated success supporting large, diverse cohorts of STEM students. Experience with orientation and transition programs. Experience improving student engagement at a large institution.

Knowledge of career opportunities related to the Biological Sciences, with demonstrated investment in cultivating student knowledge and success in career opportunities. Experience creating or overseeing new career programming.
A minimum of 7 years of experiencehigher education student services

Provides managerial leadership for student affairs operations, staff supervision, and student success initiatives. Directly supervises professional staff responsible for first-year experience and career development programs. Utilizes subject matter expertise to advise unit and school leadership. Has authority to make independent decisions about programming, staff management, and unit operations.

Skills in monitoring and assessing people, processes or services, to identify opportunities, develop creative solutions, and make continual improvements. Demonstrated success improving operational efficiency and efficacy.
Familiarity with institution-specific systems, policies, and opportunities.
Skills in project management, including setting achievable and meaningful goals, maintaining timelines, delegating work appropriately, and managing others to ensure project completion.
Strong interpersonal skills including change management aptitude, relationship cultivation, ability to effectively give constructive feedback, and excellent written and oral communication skills.
